title: KOSPI Close November 5, 2026: Falls 5.28% to 5,383.80, KOSDAQ -5.11%
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,383.80, down 5.28%, and KOSDAQ closed at 678.41, down 5.11%, as worries that a Democratic win in the U.S. midterms could tighten rules on AI data centers triggered heavy foreign selling of chip stocks. Sell sidecars were triggered on both markets, while automakers, banks and some biotech names rose.

1. Sharp sell-off — U.S. midterms and AI data center rules

KOSPI opened at 5,580.09 (-1.82%) and fell as far as 5,336.88 (-6.10%) during the session. A sell sidecar was triggered on KOSPI at 10:16 a.m. and on KOSDAQ at 2:27 p.m. Democrats winning both chambers of Congress raised concern that permitting and power-grid costs for new data centers, especially in states such as Texas and Georgia where they are concentrated, could rise. That fed worries about slower AI capital spending and weighed on chip stocks.

Foreign investors net sold about 3.39 trillion won on the KOSPI market, while individuals net bought about 2.27 trillion won and institutions about 0.84 trillion won. KOSPI's market value fell by roughly 248 trillion won in one day. On Wall Street the day before, the Dow (+3.03%), S&P 500 (+1.58%) and Nasdaq (+1.44%) all rose, but Nvidia (-3.17%) and Micron (-7.00%) fell, so semiconductors were weak on their own.

2. Semiconductors and equipment — heaviest losses

Samsung Electronics fell 7.57% to 201,500 won, SK hynix 9.46% to 1,264,000 won, SK Square 10.01% and Samsung Electro-Mechanics 15.34%. On KOSDAQ, equipment and parts makers fell hard: Simmtech (-17.97%), EO Technics (-16.20%), Wonik IPS (about -16%), Jusung Engineering (-12.21%) and Leeno Industrial (-9.53%). Some brokers noted that data centers due next year are already under construction, so the real impact would fall on projects starting after 2028.

3. Secondary batteries — giving back the prior day's gains

EcoPro BM (-7.72%), EcoPro (-7.54%) and LG Energy Solution (-2.54%) fell after the sector had been strong the day before on renewable energy hopes.

4. Automakers — hopes for EV-friendly policy

Hyundai Motor rose 3.53% to 293,500 won and Kia 5.22% to 100,800 won. Democrats are seen as more supportive of electric vehicles and renewable energy, and Hyundai has expanded production in the U.S.

5. Financials and biotech — rotation away from chips

KB Financial (+3.63%) and Shinhan Financial (+2.78%) rose, as did Celltrion (+7.50%), Samsung Biologics (+1.67%) and Alteogen (+3.68%). There was no single company-specific catalyst; the move looks like money shifting to sectors less exposed to AI and chip policy uncertainty.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 5?
KOSPI closed at 5,383.80 (-5.28%) and KOSDAQ at 678.41 (-5.11%). KOSPI touched 5,336.88 (-6.10%) at its low.

Why did Korean stocks fall so sharply?
Democratic gains in the U.S. midterms raised fears of tighter AI data center permitting and power rules, and foreigners net sold about 3.39 trillion won on KOSPI.

What level are analysts watching?
Daishin Securities pointed to 5,200 on KOSPI: a break could add selling pressure, while calmer foreign selling and a recovery in chip sentiment would be needed for a rebound.
